title: How an Accountability Partner Can Change Everything
coreMove: Engineer a social cost for skipping by binding your habit to someone whose attention you cannot ignore.

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospice nurse who keeps swearing she'll start strength training and keeps not starting
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who has privately restarted the same habit four or five times
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether her back holds up for ten more years of lifting patients
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she texts a coworker the exact words 'if I skip Tuesday's session, you get my $40' and feels the room tighten around the decision before she's even at the gym

exampleSpecs.domain: two line cooks who agreed to swap a photo of their finished prep list at 4:55pm every shift
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who thinks accountability sounds soft
exampleSpecs.stakes: the head chef's standing rule that anyone behind on prep loses the Saturday shift, which pays double
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: one cook is twenty minutes behind, sees the clock, and finishes not because he wants to but because he can already picture the empty thread at 4:56

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance illustrator and her former classmate running a weekly thirty-minute portfolio check over video
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who works alone and has watched months evaporate
exampleSpecs.stakes: a gallery submission deadline she has missed two years running
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the classmate refuses to accept 'I was busy' and asks the single concrete question 'what did you put on the page between Monday and Thursday' until the silence itself becomes the cost

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional sales manager who signed a habit contract giving his brother-in-law $200 every week he doesn't hit four gym sessions
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader skeptical that money changes anything once you have enough of it
exampleSpecs.stakes: a marriage strained by a brother-in-law he already finds smug
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the reader is walked through why the $200 matters less than the phone call where his brother-in-law says 'thanks for the check' — the social sting is doing the work the money pretended to

exampleSpecs.domain: a graduate student who told her advisor she would send 500 words on the dissertation every Friday by 5pm
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who has tried apps, timers, and journals and bounced off all of them
exampleSpecs.stakes: a fifth year of funding that depends on a chapter draft by spring
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, the Friday deadline is a private one she renegotiates with herself by Sunday; after, the same deadline is a sent email she cannot unsend, and the shift from internal to witnessed is the entire mechanism

exampleSpecs.domain: a retired firefighter and his neighbor who walk the same loop at 6:30am because each refuses to be the one who didn't show
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who suspects partners only work for ambitious thirty-somethings
exampleSpecs.stakes: a cardiologist's warning that another sedentary year will mean a stent
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: on a cold Tuesday neither of them wants to go, both are at the corner anyway, and the writer shows that the loop is not held together by motivation but by the small refusal to be seen quitting
